title: let, const, and var (scope/hoisting distinction)
learningObjectives: Explain let, const, and var (scope/hoisting distinction) and write predictable JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: let and const declare block-scoped bindings. const prevents reassignment of the binding but does not make an object immutable. var is function-scoped and has different hoisting behaviour. let and const are not usable before initialization because of the temporal dead zone.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing declarations intentionally reduces accidental reassignment and scope bugs. Prefer const by default, use let when reassignment is needed, and understand var when reading older code.
understand.analogy: A declaration creates a named storage place; scope defines where that name can be accessed.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript values, scope, and runtime behaviour follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: course and topic are const bindings; completed is reassigned with let. topic is only available inside its block.

examples.explanation: course and topic are const bindings; completed is reassigned with let. topic is only available inside its block.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page or developer console shows the values and behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Write a program with const for an unchanged binding and let for a changing counter. Try reading a block-scoped variable outside its block and observe the error.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program that uses the concept in a realistic learning-app example. Inspect values and errors in the console.
hints: Prefer const unless reassignment is required.
Do not expose private data in console output.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>let, const, and var (scope/hoisting distinction)</title></head><body>
<script>const course='HTML';let completed=0;completed+=1;{const topic='Forms';console.log(topic);}console.log(course,completed);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which declaration creates a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const creates a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned.
